goal:
PRODUCTION DEFECT in your T14 proxy apps/web/app/api/evoforge/[...path]/route.ts: isAllowed() checks prefixes on the joined decoded segments, so /api/evoforge/v1/evidence/../kernel/reservations passes the '/v1/evidence/' prefix and fetch() then normalizes the target to /v1/kernel/reservations (internal kernel API, must never be reachable from the browser). Encoded variants (%2e%2e, %2f, backslashes) behave the same.
SPEC: move the path policy into a pure module apps/web/lib/proxyPolicy.ts exporting resolveApiPath(segments: string[]): string | null and use it in the route. Return null (route answers 404 before any upstream fetch) when any segment is empty, '.', '..', contains '/', '\\', '%', a control character, or any character outside [A-Za-z0-9._~-]; then build '/' + segments.join('/') and allow only the exact paths and the prefix families already in the allowlist, where a prefix family accepts exactly ONE extra segment for /v1/evidence/{id} and /v1/events/{id}, and for /v1/commands/{id} or /v1/commands/{id}/advance. Query strings: forward only for paths that already take them (/v1/commands/{id}/advance?to_state=...). Never forward to /v1/kernel/*. Also add a tiny runnable self-check apps/web/scripts/check-proxy-policy.mjs that imports the compiled logic is NOT required; instead write the same rules as a JSON table of cases in apps/web/lib/proxyPolicy.cases.json ({path_segments, expected}) and make resolveApiPath satisfy every case (the Critic runs these cases against a live server).
check: cd apps\web && node node_modules\typescript\bin\tsc --noEmit --incremental false -p . && node node_modules\next\dist\bin\next build
